svg.title: CloudMart deployment and operations diagram
svg.desc: How CloudMart is built, deployed and run. An Azure Pipelines run builds once (tests, four app packages, the SPA, Bicep lint), then deploys infrastructure (what-if, then a subscription deployment) and the applications (zip deploys to App Service and Functions, the Payments and Shipping APIs, the SPA through the Static Web Apps CLI with a per-environment config.json, and a container image through ACR Tasks), through a workload identity federation service connection and an optional approval check. Also: parameter files and environments, how deployment outputs become app settings and config.json, deployment stacks, policy and budget, managed identities and Key Vault, schema delivery with EnsureCreated versus an EF migration bundle, rollback per service, and the alerts and health checks used after a deploy.
svg.text: How CloudMart is built, deployed and run (learning path, phases 8 and 9). The runtime is in architecture.svg, disaster recovery in continuity.svg. Grey = a lab step or a recommendation.

Secrets and identity: no keys to rotate
The service connection trades an Azure DevOps token for a short-lived Entra token on each job: no client secret.
Apps: four user-assigned managed identities, least privilege
id-cloudmart-<env>-api, -func, -pay, -ship, picked by AZURE_CLIENT_ID. Data roles grant only what each uses.
Key Vault (RBAC mode): the one application secret
PaymentGateway--ApiKey, seeded by Bicep from a @secure() parameter; read as a Key Vault reference setting.
Storage shared keys off, SQL Entra-only, Functions host storage by identity, FTP and SCM basic auth off.
By hand after the first deploy: what Bicep can't do
deploy/sql/grant-managed-identities.sql (database users, T-SQL); deploy/entra/setup-service-auth.sh (phase 16 app roles).
The one token left is the Static Web Apps deployment token: stage 3 reads it at run time and never stores it.
Schema delivery: the orders and payments databases
Today: each app creates its own schema
The API calls EnsureCreatedAsync at start-up
IF OBJECT_ID(...) IS NULL CREATE TABLE.
EnsureCreated builds the schema only in an
empty database and never updates it: a model
So the API and Payments identities hold
Build: dotnet ef migrations bundle, so the drop
carries an efbundle executable. A step between
stages 2 and 3 runs it as a deployment identity.
db_ddladmin: the apps keep data rights only.

Additive changes first (expand, then contract), so the previous build still runs while the new one deploys,
and rolling the code back doesn't need a schema rollback.
Rollback: what the current SKUs allow, and what needs more
Today, with the SKUs in the template
Needs more (a bigger SKU or a lab step)
Basic has no deployment slots: redeploy the previous run's zip.
The site restarts on deploy: expect a few seconds of errors.
S1, or Premium v3 (zoneRedundant already sets P1v3): deploy to a
staging slot, warm it up, swap. Swapping back is the rollback.
No deployment slots on Flex Consumption: redeploy the previous
Version orchestrator changes: sagas in flight replay their history
on the new code, so a breaking change fails them.
Redeploy the previous drop; stage 3 writes config.json again.
Preview environments are already enabled on the site.
Deploy with --env <name> to a preview URL first, test it, then
deploy to production. Free allows 3 preview environments, Standard 10.
Single revision mode. Images are tagged with the BuildId: set
containerImage to the earlier tag and redeploy.
Multiple revision mode: send 10% to the new revision, then 100%.
Rolling back is moving the traffic back (phase 8 lab).
Revert the commit; the pipeline applies the earlier template. Resources
a switch added stay, and no deployment rolls data back.
Deployment stack: resources removed from the template are deleted.
Data comes back from backups and point-in-time restore (phase 11).

Migration bundle with additive changes: the previous build still
works. ./efbundle <earlier migration> runs the Down steps.
